=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-Side Review of Seller Draft

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's framing — that these terms are "FINAL," "settled at principal level," "market standard," and "not to be re-opened" — is a negotiating tactic, not a constraint. I have seen no evidence the Wattlebridge principals agreed these positions. Treat the whole package as an opening draft and mark it up freely. Several "market" claims below are overstated in the Seller's favour.

---

**SPA-N-001 — General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties.
- *Buyer wants:* Higher general cap (commonly ~30–50% for a deal with this concentration risk), with fundamentals at 100%.
- *Recommendation:* **Push to ~30–40% of price.** Reason: 20% is at the low end and the Bluefen/privacy exposures justify more headroom.

**SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k (≈1%); excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- *Buyer wants:* Lower basket; "first dollar"/tipping basket so the whole amount is recoverable once triggered.
- *Recommendation:* **Accept de minimis; negotiate basket to a tipping basket and/or ~0.5%.** Reason: deductible-only recovery silently erases the first AUD 250k of every valid claim.

**SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; and a sweeper that *any* limit applies to *all* claims unless stated.
- *Buyer wants:* Minimum two full audit cycles (24 months) for general; **carve tax out to the statutory period (7 years)**.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the sweeper; set general at 24 months, tax to statutory limit.** Reason: the "applies to all Claims" drafting silently caps tax and fundamentals — unacceptable.

**SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity/title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Title/capacity at **100% of price** and **no time limit** (or statutory).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject — carve fundamentals out entirely.** Reason: capping title at 4.8m means the buyer could lose the company and recover only a fifth of the price.

**SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Silent — no carve-out; the exclusive-remedy/limitation clauses purport to cover "all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Express carve-out so **no cap, time limit, basket, knowledge qualifier or exclusive-remedy clause** applies to fraud, wilful concealment or wilful default.
- *Recommendation:* **Insist on an express fraud carve-out.** Reason: caps on fraud are unenforceable/contrary to policy and their absence is a red flag.

**SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* Deems *everything* in the data room plus all public registers disclosed against all warranties (blanket/general disclosure).
- *Buyer wants:* **Specific, indexed disclosure only**; disclosed matters must be "fairly disclosed in sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope."
- *Recommendation:* **Reject blanket disclosure; require fair/specific disclosure standard.** Reason: a document-dump deemed-disclosure defeats the warranties wholesale.

**SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for anything the Buyer/advisers knew or that was "discoverable" from data room or public records.
- *Buyer wants:* **Pro-sandbagging** (knowledge does not bar claims), or at minimum limited to actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals — never "discoverable."
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "discoverable"/constructive knowledge; delete or narrow to actual knowledge.** Reason: "discoverable" imposes an impossible diligence burden and guts the warranties.

**SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent (Clause 3/6.3)**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; consent deemed satisfied only on delivery of written consent — but **no final consent is in the data room** (Disclosure ¶2). ~30% of revenue, change-of-control clause 11.2/11.3.
- *Buyer wants:* **Condition precedent** — actual written Bluefen consent (with conditions satisfied) delivered **before Completion**.
- *Recommendation:* **Make Bluefen consent a hard CP to Completion, plus a specific indemnity.** Reason: losing ~30% of revenue on change-of-control is a core value driver, not a post-close item.

**SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released *after* Completion; no discharge in data room (Disclosure ¶3).
- *Buyer wants:* On a debt-free/cash-free basis, **repay and obtain discharge of security at/before Completion** out of the funds flow.
- *Recommendation:* **Require payoff letter + discharge of security as a Completion deliverable; deduct from proceeds.** Reason: "release following Completion" leaves the buyer holding secured debt it was told it wasn't buying.

**SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses (DD-005)**
- *Seller:* AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller," **not in the funds flow**; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unaddressed.
- *Buyer wants:* These are Completion-triggered **seller obligations** — paid by Seller or deducted as a leakage/debt-like item, **including on-costs**.
- *Recommendation:* **Treat full 420k + on-costs as Seller liability / purchase-price deduction with specific indemnity.** Reason: bonuses triggered *by the deal* are the Seller's cost, not an off-balance-sheet buyer surprise.

**SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity (Clause 11.1)**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on full payment (DD-004 cl 7.3). No proof of payment/assignment.
- *Buyer wants:* **Clean IP title** — confirmation SOW3 fully paid and Project Materials assigned, or a **broad indemnity covering loss of the IP**, not just the fee.
- *Recommendation:* **Require evidence of payment + assignment as CP, or a full (uncapped-to-fee) IP indemnity.** Reason: the risk is loss of owned IP, far exceeding the 180k fee.

**SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary," "not expected to be material," no confirmed breach — ~1,240 records (names, emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended address.
- *Buyer wants:* **Specific indemnity** covering notification costs, regulator action (OAIC/Privacy Act), remediation and third-party claims, uncapped by the general regime.
- *Recommendation:* **Demand a dedicated privacy-incident indemnity + completion of the investigation / interim findings.** Reason: NDB-scheme exposure can far exceed the "immaterial" characterisation the Seller asserts.

**SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals (DD-008/011)**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110k each (330k) are "ordinary-course"; terminability/accrual unstated.
- *Buyer wants:* Clarity on whether these are committed/unavoidable; if entered/auto-renewed pre-Completion, treat as **leakage or warrant ordinary course**.
- *Recommendation:* **Get terms (term, termination rights, timing) and a no-leakage/conduct-of-business warranty covering them.** Reason: "ordinary course" is unverified and could be a 330k committed cost.

**SPA-N-014 — Category separation (Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- *Seller:* Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature**.
- *Buyer wants:* Clear separation — general vs fundamental vs tax vs **indemnities** vs fraud, each with its own regime; indemnities and fundamentals **not** subject to general caps/baskets/time limits.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the omnibus "all Claims" drafting; ring-fence each category.** Reason: a single blanket limitation collapses every protection into the lowest common denominator.

**SPA-N-015 — Title verification (DD-012)**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced solely by the share register; disclosure notes buyer hasn't verified.
- *Buyer wants:* **Full title/capacity warranties at 100%**, plus delivery of share certificates, executed transfers, registers, and director/shareholder resolutions at Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not rely on the register alone — require title warranties (SPA-N-004 regime) + Completion deliverables.** Reason: the register is the Seller's own document; buyer needs contractual title recourse.

**SPA-N-016 — Tax / IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, blanket disclosure).
- *Buyer wants:* **Separate tax deed/indemnity** (statutory limitation, no basket, gross-up) and standalone IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, no encumbrances).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject folding tax/IP into the general regime; negotiate a tax deed and specific IP warranties.** Reason: pushing tax/IP under an 18-month, 20%-capped, blanket-disclosed regime is well below market and leaves core risks unprotected.

---

**Top priorities to hold firm on:** fraud carve-out (005), fundamentals/title regime (004), Bluefen CP (008), Riverlark discharge (009), privacy indemnity (012), tax deed (016), and deleting the "discoverable" knowledge qualifier (007). These are value- and recourse-critical and outweigh the Seller's "FINAL" framing.

Want me to draft a mark-up / issues list in reply form to send back to Seller's counsel?
